newsitem.title: USA: CME LIVE AND FEEDER CATTLE SEEN STEADY TO LOWER.
newsitem.headline: CME LIVE AND FEEDER CATTLE SEEN STEADY TO LOWER.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures alike, were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb lower, livestock analysts said.

Heavy deliveries were expected to weigh on spot August live cattle, with this week's slide in beef prices and lower cash cattle prices also seen bearish. Packers were seen lowering bids for cash cattle another $1.00 to $64 per cwt after fairly active sales Wednesday at $65, analysts said.
Back months may again show technical fund support which could hold prices steady. October held chart support before rallying Wednesday, they said.

Feeder cattle futures were expected to show renewed pressure after recovering late Wednesday to close mixed. A lower CME feeder cattle index and higher corn futures indications will likely weigh on the market, sources said. Cash feeders have been under pressure from reduced demand, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.04 at $82.27 per cwt.
Technically the market was also seen trending lower based on recent chart action, some analysts noted.
